title: Simplification: delete the pretraining-only MTP module (136-fable) from the 186-claude incumbent; plain next-token loss, identical handoff model (9,557,760 params), -48 lines
description: Idea ID: P50-family ablation (the 136-fable multi-token-prediction objective), run under program.md's simplification focus ('remove a component and show it is not needed'; the MTP module is its first named candidate): pretrain.py is 186-claude's with the MTPHead class, mtp_loss, MTP_WEIGHT and the trunk's features() split deleted, so pretraining minimises the fork's loss_on (next-token cross-entropy on proof tokens) alone; model, optimizers, schedule, init rule, token batches, compile recipe and handoff are untouched. MTP's +11.7 was measured once, at width 256 and 3,370 steps (136 vs 129); since then the model doubled in parameters and steps rose 60% into the overfitting regime, and nobody has re-tested it, so either it still earns its ~1/7 of pretraining compute and 48 lines, or expert iteration gets the same starting point from a simpler, ~15-20% faster file whose headroom a later looped or larger model can spend. 187-claude (loop-mid2) finished as a timeout before this registration; no other registration is open.
hypothesis: Two readings of 136's keep. (a) MTP is a real second supervision signal on the trunk: 136 beat 129 on all three seeds (+4/+18/+13) with a WEAKER round-1 sampler but a better eval/round-4 transfer ratio (0.594/0.604/0.575 vs 0.576/0.584/0.564). Then removing it should reverse both: a stronger RL start (round-1 sample accuracy and targets solved above 186's) and worse transfer, netting roughly -10. (b) The +11.7 was seed luck: it is 0.3-0.5 SE of a difference of 3-seed means, every follow-up on the 136 base scored below 658 (639-655 for function-identical or near-identical recipes 143/145/146-fable/149), 164's deeper module lost 37, and the token-format 056 lost 29. Then the score stays within noise of 680 and the module is dead weight. The run also adds steps (one block fewer per step), and 148/160/178/186 showed steps beyond ~4 epochs buy nothing and may overfit (val loss bottoms near 150 s), so the extra steps are not expected to help the score: they are headroom. Per seed the data order (both generators) and the embedding/readout initialisation equal 186's; the trunk's orthogonal matrices do not (186 built the MTP module before the orthogonal-init loop, which shifted the global RNG), so paired seed differences are ordinary seed pairs, not a same-init comparison. Decision rule fixed now: keep if the 3-seed mean is >= 677.0, i.e. strictly above 186's 680.33 or within 3.3 of it, the simplicity rule's '~0 with less code' calibrated to the gap the operator accepted when keeping 186 itself (-3.7); below 677.0 discard.
expected_delta: -40 to +25 vs 186's 680.3 (central -6); keep needs a 3-seed mean >= 677.0 (rule in the hypothesis). Pretraining 5,900-6,700 steps in 300 s per seed (central 6,300; 186: 5,357/5,435/5,355), ~5.2-5.9 epochs at ~1,132 batches per epoch; final main val loss 0.080-0.097 with its minimum before 200 s, train loss 0.03-0.055; held-out greedy after pretraining 0.955-0.98; handoff n_params 9,557,760 exactly. Under reading (a): round-1 RL sample accuracy above 186's 0.27 (seed 0) and round-1 targets solved above 739, with an eval/round-4 ratio below 186's. RL sampling 200-290 samples/s (handoff model unchanged), totals 1,650-2,000 s. Falsifiers: mean steps < 5,700 (the module cost less than measured); a mean below 660 confirms MTP is still worth >= 20 at width 384 (reading (a)); a mean >= 677 says it is not needed.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, the 186-claude handoff model unchanged; ALiBiGPT.forward is again one method (the features() split existed only to feed the MTP module)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 186-claude: deleted MTP_WEIGHT, class MTPHead, mtp_loss and ALiBiGPT.features (folded back into forward, same computation); pretrain() no longer builds, compiles, initialises, clips or optimises an MTP module and calls the fork's loss_on; curve points no longer carry mtp_loss. 9 insertions, 57 deletions (pretrain.py 430 -> 382 lines). Widths, depth, heads, ALiBi slopes, Muon/AdamW, schedule, init rule, token batches (TOK_BUDGET 18,432), per-block compile, CUDA-graphed Muon step and handoff unchanged.
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760, identical to 186 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107: n_params() == 9,557,760, no parameter name contains 'mtp'). No pretraining-only parameters remain: pretraining now trains exactly the 9,557,760 handed-off parameters (186 trained 11,433,344 including the 1,875,584-parameter MTP module)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; state_dict keys and shapes equal 186's
arch.kv_cache: unchanged (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check of this file: 25-token prefill then token-by-token cached decoding vs full forward, max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 at width 384

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on the 24 trunk hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms (unchanged from 186 except that the MTP module's matrices and LayerNorms no longer exist)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1; MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight: 25 Muon matrices (186: 30 with the MTP module's 5), captured as one CUDA graph as in 186
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters(), before both optimizers (186 clipped the joint norm of model + MTP module, so the trunk's share of the clip budget is now the whole)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight under Muon (25 matrices); emb.weight, biases and LayerNorms under AdamW; 9,557,760 parameters in total, all handed off

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.compile: per-block torch.compile(dynamic=True) on the 6 trunk blocks (186: 7 with the MTP block), coalesce_tiling_analysis off, undone at handoff; Muon step as one CUDA graph; fused AdamW; batch max length from host
config.init: unchanged rule: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D trunk block parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0. Embedding and readout draw the same random numbers as in 186; the trunk's orthogonal matrices draw different ones (186 constructed the MTP module between building the trunk and the orthogonal-init loop)

loss.main: the fork's train.loss_on, called directly: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions, mean over those positions (identical to the `main` term of 186's mtp_loss; val_loss, train_loss and last_loss stay comparable with 129-186)
loss.total: main only; no auxiliary loss, no pretraining-only module

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 ran from 06:33 to 06:56 BST on 2026-09-28 without ever getting an A40 (37 'no capacity' retries) and was cancelled to keep the 60-minute launch window; no pod was created. The step prediction is therefore an estimate, not a measurement: 186 ran ~20 steps/s after a 33 s setup; the MTP module is one of 7 compiled blocks plus a second ln_f/head/cross-entropy and 5 of 30 Muon matrices, and 136 measured its cost at -20.5% steps (164: -12.6% for one more MTP block).
